content.text: Jennie’s concealed daughter, Vesta, is discovered, forcing her to confess her past to Lester. He brings Vesta into their Chicago apartment, later moves the household to a Hyde Park home, and accepts Jennie’s father Gerhardt there. Social condemnation, family pressure, and his father’s will eventually compel Lester to separate from Jennie so he can reclaim his fortune. Jennie moves with Vesta to a cottage in Sandwood; after Vesta dies of typhoid, Jennie returns to Chicago. Lester, having married Letty Gerald and regained wealth, falls ill in the Auditorium Hotel and summons Jennie, confessing that she was the only woman he truly loved. He dies shortly afterward, while Jennie watches his funeral procession and train depart for Cincinnati. The appended theological chapters explain Baptism, Eucharist, and Confirmation as sacramental unions of matter and spirit, emphasizing their essentials, saving grace, regeneration, adoption, election, communion, and the laying on of hands.
